themeTitle: “Holy, Holy, Holy Is the Lord God, the Almighty”

scripture.text: After these things I looked and saw a door opened in heaven, and the first voice that I heard, like a trumpet speaking with me, was one saying, “Come up here, and I will show you the things which must happen after this.”
scripture.understanding: Μετὰ ταῦτα εἶδον, καὶ ἰδοὺ θύρα ἠνεῳγμένη ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ, “After these things I looked and saw a door opened in heaven” — εἴδω, from the see family (and the know family). After the door of 3:20 at which Jesus knocks, here is a door into heaven itself. καὶ ἡ φωνὴ ἡ πρώτη ἣν ἤκουσα ὡς σάλπιγγος, “and the first voice that I heard, like a trumpet” — the voice of 1:10. Ἀνάβα ὧδε, “Come up here” — ἀναβαίνω, to go up. Some see in this a picture of the church being taken up before the judgements that follow; most read it simply as John being called into the vision. καὶ δείξω σοι ἃ δεῖ γενέσθαι μετὰ ταῦτα, “and I will show you the things which must happen after this” — δεῖ, it must: history is in God's hands.

scripture.text: Immediately I was in the Spirit. Behold, there was a throne set in heaven, and one sitting on the throne
scripture.understanding: εὐθέως ἐγενόμην ἐν πνεύματι, “Immediately I was in the Spirit” — as in 1:10, now at a deeper level. καὶ ἰδοὺ θρόνος ἔκειτο ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ, “Behold, there was a throne set in heaven” — θρόνος: the word appears seventeen times in chapters 4–5 alone. This is the centre of everything that follows. καὶ ἐπὶ τὸν θρόνον καθήμενος, “and one sitting on the throne” — κάθημαι, to sit: God is not named; John describes only light and colour, as Ezekiel did. The throne is occupied — whatever happens on earth.

scripture.text: that looked like a jasper stone and a sardius. There was a rainbow around the throne, like an emerald to look at.
scripture.understanding: καὶ ὁ καθήμενος ὅμοιος ὁράσει λίθῳ ἰάσπιδι καὶ σαρδίῳ, “that looked like a jasper stone and a sardius” — ὅρασις, appearance. Jasper (perhaps a clear, brilliant stone like diamond; see 21:11) and sardius (deep red) were the first and last stones on the high priest's breastplate. καὶ ἶρις κυκλόθεν τοῦ θρόνου ὅμοιος ὁράσει σμαραγδίνῳ, “There was a rainbow around the throne, like an emerald to look at” — ἶρις, a rainbow: the sign of God's covenant mercy after the flood. Judgement is coming, but the throne is circled with mercy.

scripture.text: Around the throne were twenty-four thrones. On the thrones were twenty-four elders sitting, dressed in white garments, with crowns of gold on their heads.
scripture.understanding: καὶ κυκλόθεν τοῦ θρόνου θρόνοι εἴκοσι τέσσαρες, “Around the throne were twenty-four thrones” — lesser thrones around the great throne. καὶ ἐπὶ τοὺς θρόνους εἴκοσι τέσσαρας πρεσβυτέρους καθημένους, “On the thrones were twenty-four elders sitting” — πρεσβύτερος, elder. Twenty-four may combine the twelve tribes and the twelve apostles (both named on the new Jerusalem, 21:12–14): the whole people of God; or twenty-four orders of priests (1 Chronicles 24). περιβεβλημένους ἐν ἱματίοις λευκοῖς, καὶ ἐπὶ τὰς κεφαλὰς αὐτῶν στεφάνους χρυσοῦς, “dressed in white garments, with crowns of gold on their heads” — στέφανος, from the crown family: victors' wreaths, as promised to the overcomers (2:10; 3:11).

scripture.text: Out of the throne proceed lightnings, sounds, and thunders. There were seven lamps of fire burning before his throne, which are the seven Spirits of God.
scripture.understanding: Καὶ ἐκ τοῦ θρόνου ἐκπορεύονται ἀστραπαὶ καὶ φωναὶ καὶ βρονταί, “Out of the throne proceed lightnings, sounds, and thunders” — as at Sinai when God came down. This storm returns, growing, at the end of each series of judgements (8:5; 11:19; 16:18). καὶ ἑπτὰ λαμπάδες πυρὸς καιόμεναι ἐνώπιον τοῦ θρόνου, ἅ εἰσιν τὰ ἑπτὰ πνεύματα τοῦ θεοῦ, “There were seven lamps of fire burning before his throne, which are the seven Spirits of God” — λαμπάς, a torch: the Holy Spirit in His fullness (1:4; Zechariah 4).

scripture.text: Before the throne was something like a sea of glass, similar to crystal. In the middle of the throne, and around the throne were four living creatures full of eyes before and behind.
scripture.understanding: καὶ ἐνώπιον τοῦ θρόνου ὡς θάλασσα ὑαλίνη ὁμοία κρυστάλλῳ, “Before the throne was something like a sea of glass, similar to crystal” — θάλασσα: in Scripture the sea is often a picture of chaos and evil (13:1); before God's throne it is calm, transparent and still. In the new creation ‘the sea is no more’ (21:1). καὶ ἐν μέσῳ τοῦ θρόνου καὶ κύκλῳ τοῦ θρόνου τέσσαρα ζῷα, “In the middle of the throne, and around the throne were four living creatures” — ζῷον, a living being, not θηρίον, a wild beast (13:1). γέμοντα ὀφθαλμῶν ἔμπροσθεν καὶ ὄπισθεν, “full of eyes before and behind” — total awareness: nothing escapes God's notice.

scripture.text: The first creature was like a lion, and the second creature like a calf, and the third creature had a face like a man, and the fourth was like a flying eagle.
scripture.understanding: καὶ τὸ ζῷον τὸ πρῶτον ὅμοιον λέοντι, “The first creature was like a lion” — ζῷον. καὶ τὸ δεύτερον ζῷον ὅμοιον μόσχῳ, “and the second creature like a calf” — μόσχος, a young ox. καὶ τὸ τρίτον ζῷον ἔχων τὸ πρόσωπον ὡς ἀνθρώπου, “and the third creature had a face like a man” — καὶ τὸ τέταρτον ζῷον ὅμοιον ἀετῷ πετομένῳ, “and the fourth was like a flying eagle.” Ezekiel's cherubim each had all four faces. Together they may represent the noblest of all creation — wild animals, tame animals, humanity, birds — worshipping God. Later Christians linked them with the four Gospels.

scripture.text: The four living creatures, each one of them having six wings, are full of eyes around and within. They have no rest day and night, saying, “Holy, holy, holy is the Lord God, the Almighty, who was and who is and who is to come!”
scripture.understanding: καὶ τὰ τέσσαρα ζῷα, ἓν καθ᾽ ἓν αὐτῶν ἔχων ἀνὰ πτέρυγας ἕξ, “The four living creatures, each one of them having six wings” — like Isaiah's seraphim. καὶ ἀνάπαυσιν οὐκ ἔχουσιν ἡμέρας καὶ νυκτός, “They have no rest day and night” — ἀνάπαυσις, from the rest family: a pause, a break; ἡμέρα, from the time family. Their worship never pauses. Later the worshippers of the beast ‘have no rest day and night’ either (14:11) — but from torment. Ἅγιος ἅγιος ἅγιος κύριος ὁ θεὸς ὁ παντοκράτωρ, “Holy, holy, holy is the Lord God, the Almighty” — Isaiah's ‘Holy, holy, holy’, with παντοκράτωρ, the All-Ruler. ὁ ἦν καὶ ὁ ὢν καὶ ὁ ἐρχόμενος, “who was and who is and who is to come!”

scripture.text: When the living creatures give glory, honor, and thanks to him who sits on the throne, to him who lives forever and ever,
scripture.understanding: Καὶ ὅταν δώσουσιν τὰ ζῷα δόξαν καὶ τιμὴν καὶ εὐχαριστίαν, “When the living creatures give glory, honor, and thanks” — δόξα, glory; τιμή, honour; εὐχαριστία, from the pray family: thanksgiving. τῷ καθημένῳ ἐπὶ τῷ θρόνῳ, τῷ ζῶντι εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων, “to him who sits on the throne, to him who lives forever and ever” — ζάω, from the life family; αἰών, from the time family and the world family. Caesar would die; this King lives forever.

scripture.text: the twenty-four elders fall down before him who sits on the throne, and worship him who lives forever and ever, and throw their crowns before the throne, saying,
scripture.understanding: πεσοῦνται οἱ εἴκοσι τέσσαρες πρεσβύτεροι ἐνώπιον τοῦ καθημένου ἐπὶ τοῦ θρόνου, “the twenty-four elders fall down before him who sits on the throne” — πίπτω. καὶ προσκυνήσουσιν τῷ ζῶντι εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων, “and worship him who lives forever and ever” — προσκυνέω, to bow down in homage; ζάω, from the life family; αἰών, from the time family and the world family. καὶ βαλοῦσιν τοὺς στεφάνους αὐτῶν ἐνώπιον τοῦ θρόνου, “and throw their crowns before the throne” — στέφανος, from the crown family: conquered kings laid their crowns before the emperor; these victors lay theirs before God. Every reward is given back to the Giver.

scripture.text: “Worthy are you, our Lord and God, the Holy One, to receive the glory, the honor, and the power, for you created all things, and because of your desire they existed, and were created!”
scripture.understanding: Ἄξιος εἶ, ὁ κύριος καὶ ὁ θεὸς ἡμῶν, “Worthy are you, our Lord and God” — ἄξιος, deserving: the hymn opens with a title Domitian demanded for himself, ‘our Lord and God’. Only One is worthy of it. λαβεῖν τὴν δόξαν καὶ τὴν τιμὴν καὶ τὴν δύναμιν, “to receive the glory, the honor, and the power” — δύναμις, from the power family. ὅτι σὺ ἔκτισας τὰ πάντα, “for you created all things” — κτίζω: worship of God as Creator comes first (ch. 4), then worship of the Lamb as Redeemer (ch. 5). καὶ διὰ τὸ θέλημά σου ἦσαν καὶ ἐκτίσθησαν, “and because of your desire they existed, and were created!” — θέλημα, will: all things exist because God willed them.

visualMeditations.title: The Open Door in Heaven
visualMeditations.image: Picture John on his barren island looking up and seeing, in the sky, a door standing open. Through it comes the trumpet voice: ‘Come up here.’ And in a moment he is standing in the throne room of the universe.
visualMeditations.meaning: “After these things I looked and saw a door opened in heaven” (v. 1). “Behold, there was a throne set in heaven, and one sitting on the throne” (v. 2). Before John sees anything of the troubles coming on earth, he sees the throne. Every disaster in the book must be read from here.

visualMeditations.title: The Rainbow Around the Throne
visualMeditations.image: Picture a throne blazing like a jewel, red and brilliant white, with lightning and thunder flashing out of it like the storm at Sinai. And circling it all, a rainbow glowing green like emerald.
visualMeditations.meaning: “There was a rainbow around the throne, like an emerald to look at” (v. 3). “Out of the throne proceed lightnings, sounds, and thunders” (v. 5). God's holiness is terrifying; but His throne is ringed with the sign of His covenant promise. Judgement and mercy surround Him together.

visualMeditations.title: The Sea of Glass
visualMeditations.image: Picture the stormy Aegean that surrounded John on Patmos, grey and heaving. Then see, before God's throne, a sea as flat and clear as crystal, perfectly still, reflecting the light of the throne.
visualMeditations.meaning: “Before the throne was something like a sea of glass, similar to crystal” (v. 6). The chaos that rages on earth is calm before God. Nothing that frightens you is out of control in His presence.

visualMeditations.title: Crowns Thrown Down
visualMeditations.image: Picture twenty-four elders on golden thrones, wearing golden victory wreaths. As the creatures cry ‘Holy, holy, holy’, they rise, fall on their faces, take off their crowns and throw them at the foot of the throne.
visualMeditations.meaning: “The twenty-four elders fall down before him who sits on the throne, and worship him who lives forever and ever, and throw their crowns before the throne” (v. 10). “Worthy are you, our Lord and God, the Holy One, to receive the glory, the honor, and the power” (v. 11). Whatever honour we receive is only something to lay at His feet.

structure.label: The Open Door and the Throne (v. 1-3)
structure.body: John sees a door open in heaven, is called up, and in the Spirit sees a throne with One seated on it, shining like jasper and sardius, surrounded by an emerald rainbow.

structure.label: Those Around the Throne (v. 4-8a)
structure.body: Around the throne are twenty-four elders on thrones, in white with golden crowns; from the throne come lightning and thunder; seven torches burn before it, the seven Spirits; before it is a sea of glass; around it are four living creatures full of eyes, like a lion, an ox, a man and an eagle, each with six wings.

structure.label: The Unceasing Worship (v. 8b-11)
structure.body: The creatures never stop crying ‘Holy, holy, holy’ to the Lord God Almighty; whenever they give glory, the elders fall down, worship and cast their crowns before the throne, declaring God worthy because He created all things by His will.

sections.heading: The Centre of Everything
paragraphs: Chapters 4–5 are the hinge of Revelation. Before any seal is opened or any trumpet blown, John is shown the throne room of heaven. “Behold, there was a throne set in heaven, and one sitting on the throne” (v. 2). The word ‘throne’ appears seventeen times in these two chapters. Everything that happens afterward — the seals, trumpets and bowls — comes out from this throne (6:1; 8:2; 16:1). The point is unmistakable: history is not random, and evil is not sovereign. God reigns.

For the first readers this was a direct challenge. The emperor sat on a throne in Rome, surrounded by courtiers who praised him. Domitian liked to be called ‘our Lord and God’. Revelation draws back the curtain and shows the true throne room, where the elders cry, “Worthy are you, our Lord and God” (v. 11) — to the only One who deserves it.

John describes the One on the throne only by colours and light: jasper, sardius, emerald (v. 3). Like Ezekiel, he does not try to describe God's form. And around the throne is a rainbow, the sign of God's covenant with Noah that He would never again destroy the earth by flood. The judgements that follow are real, but they come from a God who keeps His promises.

sections.heading: Elders, Torches, Sea and Living Creatures
paragraphs: The twenty-four elders sit on thrones, dressed in white and wearing golden crowns (v. 4). They seem to represent the whole people of God: perhaps the twelve tribes and the twelve apostles, whose names are both written on the new Jerusalem (21:12–14). They wear the white garments and victor's crowns promised to the overcomers (3:5, 11). Some think they are angels; but either way, they show the redeemed sharing in God's rule and leading creation in worship.

Before the throne burn “seven lamps of fire... which are the seven Spirits of God” (v. 5) — the Holy Spirit in His fullness. And before the throne is “something like a sea of glass, similar to crystal” (v. 6). In the Bible the sea is often the place of chaos and the home of monsters; the beast will rise from it (13:1). Before God it is perfectly calm.

The four living creatures (vv. 6–8) combine Ezekiel's cherubim and Isaiah's seraphim. Full of eyes, they see everything; like a lion, an ox, a man and an eagle, they represent the whole created order — the strongest, the most patient, the wisest and the swiftest. Their constant song is Isaiah's: “Holy, holy, holy is the Lord God, the Almighty, who was and who is and who is to come!” (v. 8).

sections.heading: Worship of the Creator
paragraphs: The worship of chapter 4 is centred on God as Creator: “Worthy are you, our Lord and God, the Holy One, to receive the glory, the honor, and the power, for you created all things, and because of your desire they existed, and were created!” (v. 11). Everything that exists exists because God willed it. That is why everything owes Him worship, and why the beast's demand for worship (13:4) is so wicked.

Notice the rhythm: the living creatures give glory, and then the elders fall down and throw their crowns before the throne (vv. 9–10). Their crowns are real — they have won them — but they will not keep them. Conquered kings in the ancient world laid their crowns before the emperor as a sign of submission. In heaven the victors themselves acknowledge that every victory came from God.

Chapter 4 prepares for chapter 5. God is worshipped as Creator; next, the Lamb will be worshipped as Redeemer. And at the end of chapter 5 the two songs join: “To him who sits on the throne, and to the Lamb be the blessing, the honor, the glory, and the dominion, forever and ever! Amen!” (5:13).

ntConnection.heading: The Throne of Grace
paragraphs: Jesus promised His disciples a place in His Father's house: “In my Father’s house are many homes. If it weren’t so, I would have told you. I am going to prepare a place for you” (John 14:2). Revelation 4 lets John see into that house.

Stephen, as he was stoned, “looked up steadfastly into heaven, and saw the glory of God, and Jesus standing on the right hand of God” (Acts 7:55). Like John on Patmos, the suffering witness is shown the throne. And Hebrews invites every believer there now: “Let us therefore draw near with boldness to the throne of grace, that we may receive mercy, and may find grace for help in time of need” (Hebrews 4:16).

The worship of God as Creator in verse 11 is the worship of the Son too, for “All things were made through him. Without him was not anything made that has been made” (John 1:3), and “For by him all things were created, in the heavens and on the earth, things visible and things invisible, whether thrones or dominions or principalities or powers” (Colossians 1:16).

lexicon.insight: Strong's: “a stately seat ("throne"); by implication, power or (concretely) a potentate.” θρόνος appears more than forty times in Revelation — more than in the rest of the New Testament put together. Satan has a throne (2:13), the beast has a throne (13:2; 16:10), and the overcomer is promised a seat on Christ's throne (3:21). But there is only one throne at the centre, and in the end it is ‘the throne of God and of the Lamb’ (22:1, 3). The question of the whole book is: whose throne do you worship before?

Strong's: “a live thing, i.e. an animal.” ζῷον, from ζάω (to live), is a different word from θηρίον, the wild beast of chapter 13 (the King James Version called both ‘beasts’). The living creatures are the highest order of heavenly beings, like Ezekiel's cherubim and Isaiah's seraphim. They lead heaven's worship, and they summon the four horsemen (6:1–7). Life itself, in its fullest created form, exists to worship.

Strong's: “older; as noun, a senior; specially, an Israelite Sanhedrist (also figuratively, member of the celestial council) or Christian "presbyter".” πρεσβύτερος is the word for church elders (Titus 1:5) and for Israel's leaders. The twenty-four elders are a heavenly council, sitting on thrones, wearing white and golden wreaths, holding harps and bowls of incense (5:8). One of them comforts John (5:5) and another explains the vision of the white-robed multitude (7:13–14). They are the people of God, Old Testament and New, at rest and in worship.

Strong's: “intermission; by implication, recreation.” ἀνάπαυσις, from the rest family, is a pause, a break from labour. The living creatures ‘have no rest day and night’ (v. 8) — their worship never stops, not as a burden but as a joy. The same phrase returns in 14:11 for the worshippers of the beast, who ‘have no rest day and night’ — from torment. Everyone worships without ceasing; the only question is whom. Those who die in the Lord, by contrast, ‘rest from their labors’ (14:13).

Strong's: “deserving, comparable or suitable (as if drawing praise).” ἄξιος comes from a root meaning ‘to weigh’: what balances the scale. In Roman cities crowds acclaimed the emperor with shouts of ‘Worthy!’. In heaven that word is given to God as Creator (4:11) and to the Lamb as Redeemer (5:9, 12). In 5:2–4 no one in all creation is found worthy to open the scroll — until the slain Lamb steps forward. Worth in heaven is measured by the cross.

holySpiritRevelation.intro: In this chapter the Holy Spirit lifts your eyes from earth to the throne.

items.title: The Throne Is Occupied
items.body: Before John sees anything of the coming troubles, he sees “a throne set in heaven, and one sitting on the throne” (v. 2). The Spirit wants you to begin every day, every crisis and every fear here. Whatever is happening, God is on His throne. Nothing has slipped out of His hands.

items.title: Worship Is the Answer
items.body: Heaven's response to God is not anxiety or argument but worship: “Holy, holy, holy is the Lord God, the Almighty” (v. 8). The Spirit invites you to join the song of heaven now. Worship does not ignore the troubles of earth; it puts them in their proper place.

items.title: Lay Down Your Crowns
items.body: The elders throw their crowns before the throne (v. 10). The Spirit asks: what are your crowns — your achievements, gifts, reputation, successes? Lay them down before Him. Everything good you have is a gift; give Him the glory.

audit.title: The Throne Check
audit.body: When you face trouble, where do your eyes go first — to the problem, or to the throne (v. 2)?

audit.title: The Worship Check
audit.body: Is your worship mainly about what God has given you, or about who God is (vv. 8, 11)?

audit.title: The Crown Check
audit.body: What achievement or gift do you find hardest to lay at God's feet (v. 10)?

practices.title: Begin at the Throne
practices.body: For the next seven days, before you look at your phone or the news, read Revelation 4:8–11 aloud. Pray: ‘You are on the throne.’ Then bring the day's concerns to Him.

practices.title: Cast a Crown
practices.body: Write down your greatest achievement or strength. Then write beside it: ‘Worthy are you, our Lord and God, to receive the glory.’ Find a way this week to use that strength to serve someone else, quietly, for His glory alone.

prayerReflection: “Holy, holy, holy is the Lord God, the Almighty, who was and who is and who is to come! You sit on the throne of heaven, shining in light, surrounded by the rainbow of Your promise. Thunder and lightning come from Your throne, and Your Spirit burns before it like seven torches. Before You the sea is still as glass. With the living creatures I give You glory, honour and thanks, You who live forever and ever. With the elders I fall down before You, and I lay at Your feet every crown, every success, every gift You have given me. Worthy are You, our Lord and God, to receive the glory and the honour and the power, for You created all things, and by Your will they exist. When the world shakes, lift my eyes to Your throne. Open a door in heaven for me, and call me to come up and see. Amen.”

storyConnections.title: Isaiah's Vision in the Temple
storyConnections.summary: In the year King Uzziah died, Isaiah saw the Lord sitting on a throne, high and lifted up, His robe filling the temple. Seraphim with six wings called to one another, ‘Holy, holy, holy, is the LORD of Armies! The whole earth is full of his glory!’ The temple shook and filled with smoke. Isaiah cried, ‘Woe is me!’ — until a seraph touched his lips with a burning coal and his sin was atoned for. Then he heard God ask, ‘Whom shall I send?’ and answered, ‘Here I am. Send me!’ John hears the same song and sees the same throne.

storyConnections.title: Ezekiel by the River Chebar
storyConnections.summary: Among the exiles in Babylon, the priest Ezekiel saw a storm wind from the north, a great cloud with flashing fire, and in it four living creatures, each with four faces — a man, a lion, an ox and an eagle — and wheels full of eyes. Above them was a dome like crystal, and on it a throne like sapphire, and on the throne a figure like a man, surrounded by brightness like a rainbow. Ezekiel called it ‘the appearance of the likeness of the glory of the LORD’ and fell on his face. John's vision draws on Ezekiel's: in exile, God's people see that His throne is not confined to Jerusalem — it rules everywhere.

storyConnections.title: The Covenant Rainbow
storyConnections.summary: After the flood, God made a covenant with Noah and every living creature: never again would a flood destroy the earth. As a sign He set His bow in the clouds, saying that when He saw it He would remember His covenant. The rainbow around the throne in Revelation 4 reminds John that the God who is about to judge the earth is the same God who bound Himself by promise to preserve it. Judgement and mercy come from the same throne.
